sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of obstetric medicine literature
synthesis: Three further items are suggested as leads beside the retrieved records: a text-message surveillance trial, a report of midwife titration under a protocol, and a survey of smartphone ownership among postpartum women.

items.title: Text-message blood pressure surveillance after delivery for hypertensive disorders: outcomes at ten days
items.keyFindings: Text-message reporting of home readings led to more women having blood pressure measured in the first ten days after delivery.
items.notes: Lead; the year was given as text.

items.title: Postpartum antihypertensive titration by midwives under a written protocol
items.keyFindings: Midwives adjusted doses safely under a protocol, with few hypotension episodes.

items.title: Smartphone ownership and uptake of remote monitoring among postpartum women
items.keyFindings: Ownership was lower among younger mothers and recent migrants.

summary: Three leads appended; certainty left to the appraisal.
